claims.claim: The six advertised block cardinalities sum to 76.
claims.evidence: Exact arithmetic gives 6+18+16+14+16+6=76. This verifies only the stated sum, not the existence of an algorithm.
claims.witness: The independently executed checker reports shade_sum=76.

claims.claim: For any fixed allowed finite grid G and any three-Batdroid algorithm with a finite shade set Cl, the universe of configurations and its subset R_G reachable from Init(G) are finite.
claims.evidence: If G has N finite vertices and Cl has m finite shades, a legal three-Batdroid configuration uses three distinct vertices and assigns one shade to each, giving at most binom(N,3)m^3 configurations. R_G is a subset of this finite universe.
claims.witness: The bound binom(N,3)m^3 is finite for every fixed allowed G and finite Cl.
claims.search_method: Direct counting from the source definitions of grids, configurations, and collision prohibition.

claims.claim: Fix an algorithm A, an allowed grid G, and a grid vertex u. Every execution from Init(G) satisfies the PEP recurrence condition for u if and only if the subgraph induced by reachable configurations in which u is unoccupied is acyclic; equivalently, every reachable directed walk of |R_G| edges contains a configuration occupying u.
claims.evidence: A reachable u-avoiding cycle can be entered and repeated indefinitely, producing an execution that eventually omits u. Conversely, an infinite execution eventually omitting u has an infinite tail in the finite u-avoiding graph, so repetition yields a directed cycle. An all-avoiding walk of |R_G| edges has |R_G|+1 states and hence repeats; a cycle supplies avoiding walks of arbitrary length. Here a reachable walk means one whose initial state belongs to R_G.
claims.witness: Independent exhaustive testing of all 28,868 directed-graph/initial-set/occupancy-mask cases on one through three states found exact agreement between avoiding cycles and avoiding walks of |R| edges.
claims.search_method: General finite-graph proof plus exhaustive small-graph exact verification.

claims.claim: The acyclicity condition for a fixed G and u is equivalent to the existence of a bounded rank rho_u on reachable u-avoiding configurations that strictly decreases along every transition whose endpoints both avoid u.
claims.evidence: In a finite DAG, assigning each vertex the maximum length of a directed path beginning there gives a value in {0,...,|R_G|-1} and strictly decreases along every edge. Conversely, strict descent around a directed cycle would give rho(C)>rho(C), an impossibility.
claims.witness: All 13,143 acyclic avoiding subgraphs in the independent finite-graph enumeration admitted the stated longest-path rank and passed every edge inequality.
claims.search_method: Direct DAG argument plus exhaustive exact verification.

claims.claim: The at-most-76-shade construction side of the target is exactly reduced to supplying a source-model tuple A=(Cl,Init,T) satisfying the target's ambiguity, legality, and reachable-state seriality requirements together with, for every allowed grid G and every u in G, a rank rho_u of the preceding kind on the full reachable configuration graph.
claims.evidence: For a valid solving tuple, claim 2 excludes every reachable u-avoiding cycle and claim 3 supplies each rank. Conversely, with every adversarial transition included, the ranks prevent any infinite execution from having an infinite u-avoiding tail; seriality and legality ensure source-model executions continue. Quantification over every G and u is exactly the source PEP quantification. The shade bound and ambiguity remain requirements on the supplied tuple.
claims.witness: The two implications follow by applying the verified cycle and ranking equivalences independently to every allowed pair (G,u).
claims.search_method: Quantifier-by-quantifier reduction against the source definitions of algorithm, execution, ambiguity, and PEP.

claims.claim: Given the source's 77-shade upper bound, the optimality side of the target is dually reduced to proving that every source-model-valid visibility-one three-Batdroid candidate with at most 76 shades, serial on its reachable configurations, has some allowed grid G and vertex u whose reachable u-avoiding configuration subgraph contains a directed cycle.
claims.evidence: Such a cycle yields a repeatable execution violating PEP, excluding the candidate. Conversely, failure of any serial candidate to solve the universally quantified PEP supplies a grid, execution, vertex, and eventual u-avoiding tail; finiteness then extracts the required cycle. Excluding every at-most-76 candidate, together with the source's 77-shade construction, is precisely the lower-bound route to optimality.
claims.witness: Negating the source PEP definition gives existence of G, an execution, u, and a time after which u is absent; claim 2 converts this witness exactly into a reachable avoiding cycle.
claims.search_method: Logical negation of the source PEP quantifiers followed by the finite-cycle criterion.

claims.claim: For every signed orthogonal frame, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected one of the two advertised knight encounter branches lie in the finite grid, that selected branch is collision-free and swap-free and ends in K(q+r;a,r,f).
claims.evidence: Independent labeled-trace enumeration checked both branches for all 48 frames. Every displacement is idle or a unit-grid displacement, every round has three distinct destinations, and no pair reverses the same edge. Both branches end at {q+r,q+r+a,q+3r+f}=K(q+r;a,r,f). Grid membership of every displayed position makes each unit move a legal grid edge.
claims.witness: All 96 frame/branch traces passed exact endpoint, unit-move, collision, and edge-swap assertions.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive enumeration of signed coordinate-unit frames with exact integer tuples.

claims.claim: The finite-grid node-existence hypothesis in the revised knight-encounter claim is necessary in the source model.
claims.evidence: In the allowed grid {0,1,2,3}^3 with q=(1,0,0), a=(0,0,1), r=(1,0,0), and f=(0,1,0), all three staging positions are grid vertices, but q+3r+f=(4,1,0) is not. That position is required by both branches, so staging existence alone cannot make either branch a source-model trace.
claims.witness: Staging positions are (2,0,0), (3,0,0), and (3,1,0), while the required later position is (4,1,0).

claims.claim: At the advertised ordinary-transition staging configuration, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected choice lie in the finite grid, that choice is collision-free and swap-free and yields the stated diagonal frame.
claims.evidence: For each frame and ordering {d,e}={a,-r}, the e-choice ends at {q,q+d,q+e+f}=D(q;d,e,f). The d-choice followed by q→q+e and q+d→q ends at {q,q+e,q+d+f}=D(q;e,d,f). Exact checks found only unit or idle moves, distinct destinations, and no swaps.
claims.witness: All 192 combinations of 48 frames, two d/e orderings, and two outcomes passed the trace assertions.

claims.claim: The finite-grid node-existence hypothesis in the revised ordinary-transition claim is necessary in the source model.
claims.evidence: In {0,1,2,3}^3, q=(0,0,0), d=a=(1,0,0), r=(0,1,0), f=(0,0,1), and e=-r give valid staging vertices q, q+d, and q+f, but the e-choice destination q+e+f=(0,-1,1) is outside the grid.
claims.witness: The valid staging triple is {(0,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,0,1)} and the prescribed destination is (0,-1,1).

claims.claim: From the advertised outer-reset staging configuration, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected edge choice, short-axis choice, and conversion sign lie in the finite grid, that selected trace is collision-free and swap-free and ends in K(s;y,d,x).
claims.evidence: For every choice, the shift, encounter, sign-dependent correction, and handoff were reconstructed with labeled robots. Each transition uses only unit or idle moves, has distinct destinations, and contains no reversed edge. The final occupied set is {s,s+y,s+2d+x}=K(s;y,d,x).
claims.witness: All 384 combinations of 48 frames, two d/e orders, two x/y orders, and two conversion signs passed exact assertions.

claims.claim: The finite-grid node-existence hypothesis in the revised outer-reset claim is necessary in the source model.
claims.evidence: For the stated witness in {0,1,2,3}^3, all staging and shifted positions are valid, while the +d conversion requires s+2d+x=(4,1,0), outside the grid. Thus the abstract conversion is not automatically a legal source transition.
claims.witness: With q=(1,1,1), d=(1,0,0), x=(0,0,-1), and s=(2,1,1), the invalid required position is exactly (4,1,0).

claims.claim: The reset recurrence h=-f, {d,e}={a,-r}, {x,y}={h,e}, (a,r,f)->(y,d,x) is closed on the 48 signed orthogonal frames for all four choices.
claims.evidence: The vectors d,e,h are signed units on three distinct axes; x,y reorder h,e, so (y,d,x) again contains one signed unit on each axis. Independent enumeration confirmed all four successors of every frame belong to the 48-frame set.
claims.witness: All 192 recurrence edges passed the signed-orthogonal-frame membership assertion.
claims.search_method: Direct basis argument and exhaustive enumeration over six axis permutations and eight sign triples.

claims.claim: For the abstract reset recurrence, two signed orthogonal frames are mutually reachable if and only if their coordinate-sign products agree; consequently the 48-frame digraph has exactly two strongly connected components of size 24, each of directed diameter 3.
claims.evidence: Each successor permutes axes and flips exactly two vector signs, preserving the product of the three signs. Independent exact BFS from every frame reached exactly the 24 frames with the same sign product and no others. Every start had distance-layer counts 1,4,13,6, proving strong connectivity within each class and maximum directed distance 3.
claims.witness: The computed SCC sizes are [24,24], every same-sign ordered pair is reachable, and the directed diameter is 3.
claims.search_method: Invariant proof plus exhaustive directed BFS on the independently generated 48-frame graph.

claims.claim: The abstract reset recurrence admits a two-cycle under one repeated allowed choice, so closure and existential frame reachability alone cannot imply frame-wide visitation for every choice sequence.
claims.evidence: Repeatedly selecting d=-r, e=a, x=-f, y=a sends (a,r,f) to (a,-r,-f) and then back to (a,r,f). The two frames are distinct. Hence this valid choice sequence visits only two frames and disproves any universal frame-wide-visitation consequence of closure and existential reachability alone.
claims.witness: The exact checker verified this two-cycle from each of the 48 starting frames.
claims.search_method: Symbolic substitution followed by exhaustive exact-frame verification.

claims.claim: The exact target remains unresolved by this draft.
claims.evidence: The draft provides neither an explicit at-most-76-shade source-model tuple with Init and total local-view transition function T nor a universal proof for its executions. It also supplies no lower bound excluding every at-most-76 candidate. Conditional traces, frame recurrence results, and certificate reformulations establish neither target alternative.
claims.witness: No shade semantics, initialization mapping, complete transition rule, global family of ranks, or universal candidate-exclusion theorem appears in the parent.
claims.search_method: Direct completeness comparison between the parent and both alternatives in the exact source target.

target_evidence: All listed claims survive, including the finite-state cycle/rank characterization and the conditional trace and reset-frame lemmas. These are correct incomplete results, but they do not supply a 76-shade algorithm or prove a 76-shade impossibility. The parent's claimed resolution is PARTIAL and its writeup expressly disclaims full target coverage, so that claim is accurate rather than overstated.
